text:
Mira (new-hire): hey folks, onboarding question — I'm wiring up integration tests for the auth-proxy feature. Should I use my personal hosted key, a sandbox key, or a team service key so tests never touch prod? Also our CI spawns 8 parallel runners, worried about hitting quotas/429s.

sam-devex: short answer: use a sandbox service key tied to the team. personal keys are for local dev only. Service sandbox keys are rotatable and easier to manage in CI.

Mira (new-hire): how do I request one? I don’t have console access yet.

ops-jen: open a request in #help with your repo name + which org team (e.g., eng-platform). We create a sandbox service key and add it to the project's secrets store. Tag the key with the pipeline id so we can track usage.

Mira (new-hire): cool — any best practices for avoiding throttles from parallel jobs?

infra-alfie: two main patterns: 1) client-side rate limit and shared token across runners, 2) one token per runner/incremental concurrency. We usually prefer a single service key + per-job local limiter so you don't exceed burst quotas. Add exponential backoff + jitter on 429.

ops-jen: also monitor response headers. we return `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and sometimes `Retry-After`. Respect those and drop retries if the test can be skipped (failing fast vs noisy reruns).

Mira (new-hire): can you paste a tiny example for CI secret + curl so I can copy/paste?

sam-devex: sure — set a CI secret named `REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY`. locally `export REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY=sk-sandbox-xxxx`. example curl (non-streaming):

```
export REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY="sk-sandbox-xxxxx"
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-mini","input":"ping"}' \
  https://api.redwood-inference.dev/v1/generate
```

sam-devex: for CI tests we prefer deterministic responses — stub generation calls for unit tests and run one dedicated integration job against sandbox for full-stack checks.

Mira (new-hire): streaming caused flakes for me locally. Should I disable streaming in CI?

infra-alfie: yes, disable streaming for parallel CI jobs. If you need to validate streaming framing, run a single serial e2e job or use the dev proxy that simulates chunked responses.

security-ron: security reminder: never commit keys. rotate sandbox service keys on role changes or quarterly. Store keys in our Vault/CI secrets manager and add ACLs so only the pipeline can read them. If you suspect exposure, revoke the key immediately via Console and ping security.

ci-bot: FYI: current sandbox quota for `eng-platform` is 150 rps and 8k tokens/minute. If you expect sustained higher concurrency, open a #help ticket with expected qps and token profile so we can evaluate a temporary bump.

devex-bot: dev tip: use `devex/tools/redwood-sim` to mock rate limits and Retry-After behavior in CI to ensure your retry/backoff logic is solid.

Mira (new-hire): perfect, thanks everyone. I'll open the help ticket with concurrency details and request the service sandbox key. tagging @sam-devex and @ops-jen to help wire it into our pipeline. :party:
